newsitem.title: CONGO: Fighting in Zaire capital kills dozens - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Fighting in Zaire capital kills dozens - witnesses.

text.p: The bodies of Zairean soldiers and civilians killed in an overnight shootout with rebels littered neighbourhoods of the capital Kinshasa on Sunday, witnesses said.
Following an International Red Cross truck picking up the bodies, one witness saw 40 collected from different neighbourhoods during one hour on Sunday morning.
Most of the dead were soldiers who went on a last-minute looting spree on Saturday night, the witness said.
"Within the space of one hour we saw around 40 bodies picked up. The rebels do not want to hear of looting. They killed one soldier looting literally in front of us," the witness said.
In the heavily populated neighbourhood of Bandale in Central West Kinshasa, at least 15 bodies littered a 100-metre (yard) stretch of road on Sunday morning, residents said.

"There were 15 bodies on just one 100-metre stretch of road in Bandale. Most of them were soldiers known in the neighbourhood but there were also two people killed while driving in the night," the witness from Bandale said.
Rebels entered the Camp Tshatshi military barracks where the last remnants of President Mobutu Sese Seko's elite presidential guard continued overnight resistance, on Sunday morning, witnesses said.
Most of the guardsmen who are traditionally recruited from Mobutu's Ngbandi tribe surrendered after long negotations with rebels during the morning.
A group of about 20 of the Israeli-trained soldiers were still refusing to hand over weapons and were holed up in a building close to Mobutu's Tshatshi residence, witnesses said.
A Western diplomat said some Belgian houses were looted in citywide looting overnight but he added that so far there had been no reports of expatriate deaths.
In the wealthy Western neighbourhood of Binza, looting continued until around 3 a.m. when rebels entered the area, residents said.
A group of loyalist soldiers were still resisting rebels there on Sunday, they said.
